title: Xcode 16.4 changelog
content_html:
This stack is frozen and no longer receives updates, as described in the stack update policy. It's deprecated and will be removed on Sep 15, 2027. Migrate to the Xcode 26.0 stack to receive tool updates and security patches.

Check out the stack report page for a snapshot of what is currently installed.

Updates #

Notice v2026-10-26 #

This stack is [frozen](https://devcenter.bitrise.io/en/infrastructure/build-stacks/stack-update-policy.html) and doesn't receive updates, so it still trusts the [compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/). Tools on macOS check certificates against one of three trust stores, and each one is affected differently: - **Homebrew trust store** (Homebrew's `ca-certificates` package): used by tools built against Homebrew's OpenSSL, such as `wget`. Run `brew upgrade ca-certificates` in the beginning of your builds to install the fixed package and untrust the compromised CAs. - **macOS system trust store** (`/etc/ssl/cert.pem`): used by the curl that ships with macOS and the tools built on it, such as `git`. `brew upgrade ca-certificates` doesn't change this file. Apple will fix it in a macOS update, which this stack won't receive. Until then, follow [Apple's instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/149555) in the beginning of your builds to remove the compromised root CAs from the file. - **Apple's Security framework** (the keychain): used by Xcode and other tools that rely on Apple's networking APIs. Apple's Security framework does perform updates to certificate configuration data, but the timing of these updates is not guaranteed to happen early in the build (for example, before the first steps download their dependencies). The preinstalled versions of Java, Node.js, pip, fastlane and other tools that bundle their own root certificates stay affected regardless of the trust stores above. Migrate to a supported stack, such as [Xcode 26.0](https://stacks.bitrise.io/stack_reports/osx-xcode-26.0.x/), to receive tool updates and security patches. See the [migration guide](https://stacks.bitrise.io/announcements/deprecating-xcode-16.x-stacks/).

Stack update v2026-09-25 (released 2026-09-28) #

  • New preinstalled CLI tools: 1password-cli, sentry-cli

Stack update v2026-08-13 (released 2026-08-17) #

  • macOS update 15.4.1 → 15.7.9 to address Screen Sharing vulnerability
  • Bitrise CLI upgrade: 2.40.7 → 2.42.2
  • Bitrise guest agent upgrade: 2.2.0 → 2.10.1
  • OpenSSH upgrade: 9.9p1 → 9.9p2

Stack update v2026-06-30 (released 2026-06-30) #

  • New preinstalled CLI tools: ffmpeg, tmux, uv
  • Android SDK component ndk;27.1.12297006 is now preinstalled, matching the current React Native default

Stack update v2026-02-20 (released 2026-03-03) #

  • The preinstalled Ruby versions are now built with --enable-shared. The --disable-shared option was required for compatibility with a past version of Xcode, but it is no longer necessary. Using --enable-shared allows Ruby gems with native extensions that depend on the shared Ruby library to work properly.

Stack update v2026-01-15 (released 2026-01-19) #

  • Lix (Nix-like) is preinstalled and configured

Stack update v2025-09-15 (released 2025-09-22) #

  • ripgrep (rg) is preinstalled and available to other tools

Stack update v2025-08-11 (released v2025-08-12) #

  • Added: iOS 18.6 simulator runtime (iOS 18.5 remains installed, but you should try 18.6 if you experience stability issues)
  • pre-commit CLI is now preinstalled
  • licenseplist CLI is now preinstalled
  • crowdin CLI is now preinstalled

Stack update v2025-07-07 (released 2025-07-14) #

  • From now on, you can expect the simulator device Bitrise iOS default to be paired with an Apple Watch device

Stack update v2025-05-29 (released 2025-05-29) #

Initial stack release
